messages:
alex: Trying to profile the KV-cache stall regression but nsys won't attach inside our rootless sandbox. CUPTI error: `CUPTI ERROR 11: cuptiActivityEnable failed`

maria: ugh, rootless + CUPTI is a classic pain. can you paste the exact nsys command and the brief error output?

alex: command:
```
nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,cudnn --output=run1 ./bin/serve -model x
```
error snippet:
```
CUPTI error: CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_DEVICE (11) at libcuptiActivity.so
Unable to open device /dev/nvidiactl: Permission denied
```

ben: two quick things to check: 1) are device nodes mounted into the sandbox? rootless containers often don't have /dev/nvidia* mapped. 2) driver/CUPTI mismatch — CUPTI from CUDA 12 with a driver < 520 will misbehave.

maria: +1 to ben. also rootless user namespaces break the nsys attach flow because it needs to load the CUPTI shared object into the target process. no CAP_SYS_ADMIN = no fun.

alex: we do mount /dev/nvidia0 but it's owned by root:video and rootless user can't open ctl. i tried LD_PRELOAD pointing to host CUPTI lib and got further: nsys starts but timeline shows big kernel fallbacks and the kvcache hotpath has long memcpy stalls.

ben: can you share the timeline excerpt? even a few lines like which kernels fired. sometimes cuBLAS/cuDNN symbol mismatch causes runtime to choose a reference GEMM kernel (slow) instead of the optimized one.

alex: pasted small excerpt from the .qdrep converted to text:
```
Timeline: kernel 0x7f7abc: ncclAllReduce (slow path)  12.4ms
Timeline: kernel 0x8a8bcd: matmul_generic_kernel  9.7ms  <-- unexpected
Timeline: memcpy H2D  1.1ms  (sync)  stalls KV cache
```

maria: that matmul_generic_kernel screams kernel-selection mismatch. what CUDA/cuDNN versions on the host vs inside sandbox?

alex: host: driver 525.60, CUDA toolkit 12.2 (CUPTI lib from /usr/local/cuda-12.2/extras/CUPTI/lib64). sandbox: user namespace with CUDA headers but no system driver. i did a quick test by mounting host /usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64 and `export LD_LIBRARY_PATH` — then nsys attach works but perf regression still there.

ben: mounting CUPTI helps attach but doesn't fix kernel selection. likely the userland libraries inside sandbox are a different cuBLAS/cuDNN ABI, so runtime falls back. two options: 1) profile on the host (ssh into node) to avoid rootless isolation, 2) run rootful container with nvidia-container-runtime, or 3) ensure exact matching of host driver + toolkit libs inside sandbox (risky).

ops-bot: CI note: reproducible perf regression observed on 2027-03-05 nightly on dedicated-gpu-4 (nsys 2023.4). baseline before update: avg matmul 3.2ms, after: 9.7ms.

alex: i can do host profiling but the reproduce path is easier inside dev sandboxes for engineer convenience. any lightweight workaround to let nsys attach in rootless without giving full privileges?

maria: two hacks we've used: 1) run a small privileged helper on the host that creates a proxy endpoint (tty/socket) that the sandboxed process can request to load CUPTI — messy. 2) use `nsys profile --capture-range=cudaDriver` with NVTX markers around the hot region and run the actual trace on host via remote collection (start/stop hooks) — less info but often enough to see kernel selection.

ben: also try `--sample` mode in nsys (lower fidelity) to avoid needing full CUPTI activity. it sometimes bypasses the attach flow.

alex: thanks — i'll try host-run and the NVTX remote capture trick. for immediate blocking we landed a telemetry guard: if we detect sandboxed attach failure, fall back to timeline sampling + additional kvcache counters and flag the run as "partial-profile".

ci-bot: attached artifact: https://artifacts.internal/redwood/profiles/1813456789-run1-qdrep (partial).

maria: great. when you have the host trace, post the kernel list — if matmul_generic persists, we'll bisect the cuBLAS/cudnn versions and check our kernel selection tables. :thumbsup:
